item.title: Chocolate eyeball candy sold at Marshalls, TJ Maxx recalled
item.description: The recalled candy, sold under the brand "Crystal Temptations," was distributed in 13 states.

item.title: Lindsay Clancy trial jury resumes deliberations as mistrial potential grows
item.description: It appears the Lindsay Clancy murder trial in Massachusetts could end in a mistrial.

item.title: Hegseth favors Sean Parnell for Army secretary, sources say
item.description: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth has told people close to him that Sean Parnell would be his top choice for secretary of the Army, several senior officials told CBS News.

item.title: Iran ignores Trump's warning, claims new attacks on bases used by U.S.
item.description: Iran claims new strikes against American forces in Kuwait and the UAE as the Pentagon says it's looking into reports of a U.S. strike hitting a wedding party.

item.title: Voters are "pissed about the economy," former Obama aide analyzes midterms
item.description: Most midterm primaries have already passed, yielding data and trends that inform how general elections could go. Former Obama aide Ravi Gupta joins CBS News with more on how Democrats and Republicans are performing in the 2026 midterms so far.

item.title: U.S. layoffs in August fell to their lowest level in 4 years
item.description: Job cuts around the U.S. have declined this year even amid signs that hiring is weakening.

item.title: AI interviews rolling out for some federal government hires, sources say
item.description: The federal government will shift into using artificial intelligence in the interview process for some job applicants in the coming days, according to U.S. officials.

item.title: "Monsters of God" creators on the deep, dark world of reptile smuggling
item.description: Eric Goode, the director and executive producer of HBO's "Monsters of God" and Jeremy McBride, an executive producer, sit down with "CBS Mornings" to talk about the show and what they hope audiences will learn.

item.title: Texas slammed by Edouard's aftermath
item.description: Heavy rains continued to slam Texas in the aftermath of Edouard. Jason Allen reports.

item.title: Leon Black defies House subpoena, sues committee over Epstein probe
item.description: Leon Black, a former close associate of Jeffrey Epstein, was subpoenaed in June after he abruptly left a voluntary appearance before the House Oversight Committee.

item.title: Mother of USS Abraham Lincoln sailor "so relieved" son has arrived in Thailand
item.description: The USS Abraham Lincoln pulled into port in Thailand for some rest and relaxation after 286 days at sea.

item.title: What happens to money from pending deposits when your bank account is frozen?
item.description: A frozen bank account can leave incoming money in limbo. Here's what could happen to your pending deposits.

item.title: "48 Hours" show schedule
item.description: "48 Hours"' uncovers the narrative behind true crime cases with unmatched reporting and suspense.

item.title: "Shark Tank" judge Daniel Lubetzky on the 4 crucial skills for building a business
item.description: "Shark Tank" judge and KIND Snacks founder Daniel Lubetzky joins "CBS Mornings" to discuss his new podcast, "Build or Break," where he sits down with fellow entrepreneurs and industry disruptors.

item.title: Good Good Golf CEO resigns after furor over Callaway ad
item.description: The top two executives at digital marketing company Good Good Golf are leaving after a controversial ad was panned as sexist.

item.title: Exclusive discounts from CBS Mornings Deals
item.description: On this edition of CBS Deals, we show you items that will help improve your everyday lifestyle. Visit cbsdeals.com to take advantage of these exclusive deals today. CBS earns commissions on purchases made through cbsdeals.com.

item.title: Hack exposes more than 150 million U.S. and Canadian driver's licenses on dark web
item.description: The FBI is investigating a recent hack that put more than 150 million U.S. and Canadian driver's license scans for sale online. Chris Krebs, former director of the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency joins with more.

item.title: USS Lincoln crew reaches land after long, grueling deployment
item.description: USS Abraham Lincoln sailors were finally able to disembark after 286 days at sea and reports of dire conditions aboard. CBS News' Anna Coren has more.

item.title: Is charged-off credit card debt easier to settle?
item.description: A charge-off changes how a credit card company treats your debt, but what does it mean for your settlement options?

item.title: Volatile gas prices fuel inflation fears
item.description: Oil prices are reacting to developments in the war in Iran, with ripple effects felt throughout the stock market. CBS News' Kelly O'Grady explains more.

item.title: Norah O'Donnell returning as co-host of "CBS Mornings"
item.description: Norah O'Donnell​ is returning as co-host of "CBS Mornings" alongside Gayle King and Nate Burleson.

item.title: Trump's plan to propel battleground Republicans as Iran war stretches on
item.description: President Trump invited Republicans to a dinner at the White House Rose Garden to discuss his plan to boost voter turnout ahead of the midterms. This comes as fighting between Iran and the U.S. has ramped up again. CBS News' Olivia Rinaldi has more.

item.title: From the archives: Gloria Steinem announces fight for abortion rights in New York
item.description: Gloria Steinem has died at 92. The pioneering leader in the women's liberation movement addressed an initiative in the 1970s that would have interfered with access to an abortion if signed by Governor Nelson Rockefeller. In this archive clip, Steinem protested the Donovan-Crawford Bill and called for national support for her cause.

item.title: Suspect in downtown Minneapolis mass shooting was facing eviction
item.description: The man suspected of killing two people and injuring six others in a mass shooting at a downtown Minneapolis apartment complex Wednesday was facing eviction after a string of incidents including assault and allegedly showing a gun to apartment management, according to court documents.

item.title: Military personnel told last month to stop calling Iran conflict "Operation Epic Fury"
item.description: The Pentagon says "Operation Epic Fury" ended on May 5, after an Air Force email last month told service members to stop using the name for ongoing Iran operations.

item.title: Gloria Steinem, trailblazing figure in women's liberation movement, dies at 92
item.description: Gloria Steinem, co-founder of Ms. Magazine, was a leader in raising awareness about gender equality and violence against women, and for promoting inclusion, representation and social justice for women and girls.

item.title: Hillary Clinton on Gloria Steinem: "One of the architects" of women's equality
item.description: Former Secretary of State Hillary Clinton remembered activist Gloria Steinem as "one of the architects of the entire structure of women's equality," while encouraging young women to lift up each other.

item.title: U.S. sinks second "floating refueling station" used by alleged drug traffickers
item.description: The U.S. military intercepted and sank a vessel that was allegedly being used to support at-sea drug trafficking by the Ecuadorian criminal organization Los Choneros, officials said.

item.title: USS Abraham Lincoln docks in Thailand after more than 9 months at sea
item.description: The USS Abraham Lincoln aircraft carrier has docked in eastern Thailand after its grueling deployment in the Middle East.

item.title: Newsom may veto bill giving California high-speed rail watchdog more power, sources say
item.description: Critics called it the "anti-transparency" bill. Newsom quietly enacted the controversial part and may now veto the part the rail watchdog says he needs, sources tell CBS California.
